primary.key: Excellent Savitar hath mounted up on high for you, ye sure and careful Guides. Bipeds and quadrupeds, with several hopes and aims, and birds have settled to their tasks.
primary.s: A hymn to all the gods, seeking their gifts at dawn, noon and dusk, here greets the rising sun; Sāyaṇa, commentary on 8.27.12, reads the creatures’ tasks as some men beginning the Agnihotra, others praising the gods, and beasts roaming to graze.
primary.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.27.12, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.२७, revision 208927 (2019)

basis.words: स्वस्वकार्येषु निविशन्ते । सूर्य उदिते केचन पुरुषा अग्निहोत्रादिकं कुर्वन्ति केचन देवताविषयं स्तोत्रं कुर्वते । पश्वादयस्तृणादिभक्षणार्थं सर्वत्र संचरन्ति ।
basis.gloss: They settle each to his own work. When the sun has risen, some men perform the Agnihotra and the other rites, some make praise addressed to the gods; cattle and the other beasts roam everywhere to eat grass and the like.

standby.key: NOT one of you, ye Gods, is small, none of you is a feeble child: All of you, verily, are great.
standby.s: A four-verse hymn to the Three-and-Thirty opens in praise before asking shelter and to be kept on the fathers’ path; Sāyaṇa, commentary on 8.30.1, reads the gods as all of one age and ever young, and ‘great’ as greater than all that exists.
standby.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.30.1, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.३०, revision 201714 (2019)

basis.words: युष्माकं मध्ये कुमारोऽपि नास्ति । किंतु सर्वे यूयं सवयसो नित्यतरुणा भवथ । … सर्वस्माद्विद्यमानात् पृथिव्यामपि ये महान्तस्ते सतोमहान्त इत्युच्यन्ते ।
basis.gloss: Among you there is not even a youth; rather all of you are of equal age, ever young … those who are great beyond all that exists, even on earth, are called satomahāntaḥ (great beyond what is).

primary.key: Agni bestows all vital power even as each man supplicates. He brings the Vasus strengthening gifts, and grants delight, in rest and stir, for every calling on the Gods.
primary.s: A hymn to Agni, each verse wishing all the others away, praises him as the gods’ messenger; Sāyaṇa, commentary on 8.39.4, reads the delight as happiness born of calm and of the senses’ objects, and takes Agni as doing all, whichever god is invoked.
primary.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.39.4, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.३९, revision 275528 (2020)

basis.words: “शं शान्तिनिमित्तं "योः विषययोगजनितं “च “मयः सुखं “दधे करोति । “विश्वस्यै “देवहूत्यै सर्वस्मै देवानां ह्वानाय च भवति । यः कश्चनापि देवो यदि हूयते अग्निरेव सर्वं करोतीत्यर्थः ।
basis.gloss: He makes happiness, śam, arising from tranquillity, and yoḥ, born of contact with the objects of sense. He is there for every invocation, for the calling of all the gods: whatever god is invoked, it is Agni alone who does it all; that is the meaning.

standby.key: Thou helpest one to power, and one thou hast not helped, O Indra, Lord of Strength, with all thy saving aid.
standby.s: A hymn calling Indra to the Soma poured at noon lists his lordship over the world; Sāyaṇa, commentary on 8.37.6, reads him as existing for the world’s strength and guarding all who take refuge, while no one guards him.
standby.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on 8.37.6, sa.wikisource ऋग्वेदः सूक्तं ८.३७, revision 191734 (2019)

basis.words: “त्वं “क्षत्राय जगतो बलाय भवसि । “अवसि आश्रितान् रक्षसि । “त्वं “न “आविथ केनापि न रक्ष्यसे ।
basis.gloss: You are for kṣatra, the strength of the world. You protect (avasi) those who have taken refuge with you. You were not protected (na āvitha): by no one are you protected.
